title: Korea's privacy regulator issues draft decree on using personal data for AI development, open for comment
date_note: Boannews published the notice on 23 November, the day the comment period is said to start.
geo_basis: country: a national regulator in South Korea
summary: Boannews reports that the Personal Information Protection Commission drafted an amendment to the Enforcement Decree of the Personal Information Protection Act. It would allow lawfully collected personal information to be used for AI development under set conditions, with safeguards such as a responsible officer, access controls and destruction once no longer needed. Public comment runs from 23 November to 4 January.
plain: Korea's privacy regulator proposed rules letting lawfully collected personal data be used to develop AI under safeguards. The public can comment until 4 January, Boannews reports.
exec: Boannews reports the draft would add safeguards and risk assessments for higher-risk uses of personal data in AI development.

validation.note: Boannews and Daily Security (two publishers) each report the commission's draft decree amendment allowing personal data use for AI development with safeguards; the commission's own page was not read.

review.note: Compared title, date, comment period 23 Nov-4 Jan, safeguards and risk assessment with Boannews report
